newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move which pits Woolworths Ltd against Australia's largest wholesaler and fourth-largest food retailer Davids Ltd, Woolworths group managing director Reg Clairs revealed yesterday the giant retailer is planning to become a major player in the A$11 bilion-a-year wholesaling and food service market. Page 1.

In a move expected to raise up to A$200 million, United States oil giant Exxon Corp, which operates the giant Bass Strait oil and gas fields, has announced it plans to quit its Australian base metals and coal interests in a long-awaited move to concentrate on its energy businesses in the country. Page 17.

Reinsurance Australia Corporation managing director Mike Kelly has revealed that, following a 21 per cent boost in gross written premiums to A$527.3 million in the year to December 31, the group has set its sights on becoming one of the top-20 reinsurance companies in the world within three years. Page 17.

Following a private hearing of the Corporations and Securities Panel yesterday - only the panel's second matter and the first since it was reformed to allow private hearings - the conduct of agricultural products group Pivot Nutrition's takeover of Tasmanan flour miller Gibson's Ltd was declared unacceptable. Page 17.

After posting an unaudited 16 per cent in rise in net profit to A$2.2 million for the half-year to December, thanks largely to the summer success of Emma, film and television distributor the Becker Group Ltd has predicted continued growth in its key markes for the full year, with increased television production hoped to underpin further strong results. Page 19.

Despite recording a 32 per cent drop in interim profit yesterday, Perth-based industrial conglomerate Futuris Corp Ltd says it is on track to report full-year earnings of A$42 million as outlined in its takeover for Elders Australia Ltd and believes the building cycle and rural economy will start to move in its favour later this year. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In an ambitious bid to take market share from Davids Ltd, which dominates the national wholesale grocery market outside of Western Australia, Reg Clairs, the chief executive of retail giant Woolworths Ltd, yesterday confirmed the group is poised to expand into the A$10 billion-a-year wholesale grocery distribution business. Page 19

Telecommunications industry players, including general manager of Telstra's international carrier business, John Hibbards, predicted yesterday the landmark World Trade Organisation agreement on liberalising the global telecommunications industry, signed a the weekend, will present major investment opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region for Australian carriers and exporters. Page 19.

At a time when the coal industry is experiencing difficulties, oil and gas multinational Exxon Corp, which owns the oil and gas assets of Esso Australia Ltd, has announced it is selling its Australian coal and base metals interests, valued at an estimated A$250 million. Page 19.

On the eve of an Indonesian Government-imposed deadline for Bre-X Minerals Inc and Canadian miner Barrick Gold Corp to resolve a dispute over Indonesia's massive Busang gold mine, US giant Freeport McMoRan Copper & Gold FXN.AX has signed a deal with Bre-X to devlop the mine. Page 19.

In a move which increases the potential for resolution of the A$1.1 Century project issue before it moves beyond the preliminary stages of arbitration, Century Zinc Ltd has indicated it may consider a full agreement by Gulf Aborigines to develop the projet, but will not be involved in any further discussions on the controversial issue. Page 21.

Despite a 28 per cent drop in revenue to A$18.6 million, film producer and distributor Becker Group Ltd - one of four production houses listed on the Australian share market - lifted net profit 15.7 per cent from A$1.92 million to A$2.23 million in the Deember 31 half-year, with directors confident of continued growth in the second half. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

After posting another strong increase in net profit to A$147.5 million for the December half, achieved despite troubled times over the Christmas period, retailer Woolworths outlined plans yesterday to expand into the wholesale grocery supply and food servce markets. Page 25.

Employees of transport, manufacturing, building and computer services are expected to be prime targets for conversion to contractor status following a High Court decision last Friday to deny an appeal from the Tax Office on the contractor status of couries. Contractors can claim tax benefits for self-employed superannuation contributions while the employer avoids paying compulsory superannuation and holiday leave. Page 25.

The World Trade Organisation agreement to deregulate the telecommunication market allows Telstra to grab a share of the expanding South-East Asian market in competition with some of the world's largest telecommunication companies. Telstra's domestic earnings will come under pressure when foreign companies are allowed into the domestic market from July 1. Page 25.

A 31 per cent increase in net profit for the year to December for Reinsurance Australia Corporation was higher than prospectus forecasts and struck on a 21 per cent rise in gross written premium income to A$527.3 million. The increase in profit to A$66.6 illion reflected a low worldwide level of claims and offshore branch profitability. Page 27.

Becker Group's interim net profit was lifted by 15.7 per cent to A$2.2 million by a strong performance in TV production and the box-office success of the film Emma. The bottom-line rise came despite a 27.8 per cent fall in total revenue from A$25.7 millio to A$18.55 million. Page 27.

Property Council of Australia figures show office vacancies in Australia's central business districts are down by 12.4 per cent, with Sydney vacancies down to 7.5 percent from 10.4 per cent six months ago. National vacancies are at their lowest for six yers, but rents are not high enough to justify new construction in most markets. Page 27.
THE AGE

Woolworths has moved to break Davids monopoly on the Wholesale grocery industry by establishing a new warehousing and distribution arm from its Australian Independent Wholesalers business. The move capitalises on discontent among independent retailers wit Davids, and coincides with the announcement of a 8.62 per cent increase in interim net profits for Woolworths to A$147.5 million. Page C1.

The Corporations and Securities Panel has not frozen superphosphate giant Pivot's bid for Tasmanian miller Gibson's, despite finding Pivot's conduct in the takeover bid unacceptable. The panel found that a decision by a Pivot subsidiary to end a supply arangement with Gibson's was motivated by the takeover bid. The panel urged Pivot to increase its A$6 a share offer. Page C1.

A Price Waterhouse survey has found one-third of smaller public floats fail to get within 15 per cent of their projections in their first year. From January 1992 to the end of 1996 companies with less than A$100 million market capitalisation underperforme the broader industrial market by around 30 per cent on average. Page C3.

Australia's national telecommunications carrier Telstra has set its sights on the Asian market following the World Trade Organisation's deregulation deal struck on the weekend. Telstra is now interested in the Japanese market and entering into Singapore, ut will run into competition from BT/MCI. Page C3.

Futuris Corp recorded a A$22 million net interim profit, in line with full-year forecasts. The profit was struck on a A$1.2 billion rise in sales revenue and aided by a sound performance in its automotive components division and its newly acquired interes in rural group Elders Australia. Futuris Corp is moving towards compulsory acquisition of Elders which is expected to be completed at the end of March. Page C3.

Mirvac Property Trust's general manager Rob Hattersley said Mirvac is still on track to deliver a forecast distribution yield of 11.4 cents a unit despite a softening in retail property yields which led to a net reduction of A$13.03 million across the trust's total portfolio. Mirvac reported a distribution of 5.65 cents for the six months to 31 December. Page C3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
